guidance: A rule-composition aid, not a compliance guarantee: auditd evaluates the loaded set in order, so an earlier never rule or a missing arch field changes what is recorded. Check the machine's own loaded rules with auditctl -l after adding one.
method: Every rule is composed in the syscall form, which audit.rules(7) recommends over the deprecated -w watch: -a always,exit, then the arch field, then either -F path= or -F dir= with -F perm=, or -S with the chosen calls and one -F field comparison, then -k. The action and list are fixed at always and exit because file watches and syscall filters are both evaluated on the exit list. The architecture choice writes one line for b64 or b32, two lines (b64 then b32) for both, because syscall numbers differ between the ABIs, and no arch field for none, which auditctl then applies to every system call. Access types are read, write, execute and attribute change, emitted in the order rwxa after duplicates are dropped; a directory watch uses dir= and follows the subtree to the bottom, stopping at mount points. A path must be absolute, cannot be / and cannot contain whitespace, quotes or backslashes. System call names are lowercase letters, digits and underscores, separated by commas or spaces and deduplicated in the order given; any well-formed name is accepted because the valid set is kernel and architecture specific. Filter fields are the login uid, uid, euid, gid, pid, ppid, executable path, exit success and exit errno; exe, success and exit accept only = and !=, success only 0 or 1, exit an errno name such as -EACCES or a number, id fields take up to ten digits and at most 4294967295, and auid alone also takes unset or -1, both of which print as unset. With the unset option on, an auid comparison gains -F auid!=unset, the idiom audit.rules(7) uses to leave out processes without a login session. Keys are optional, at most 31 characters, and limited here to letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens so the rule stays one shell-safe line. The result reports each rule line, the field count including arch, the character count, and warnings for a missing key, a missing arch field, -S all and an unchecked unset exclusion.
